fact: TTCL, through the National ICT Broadband Backbone, and Burundi Backbone System agreed to raise connectivity capacity to Burundi from 4Gbps to 10Gbps, so a terrestrial Tanzania-Burundi link was already carrying 4Gbps; reported by Tech Africa News on 9 September 2026.

ARCT's 2020 ICT indicators report (July 2021) states Burundi has access to submarine cables (EASSy, SEACOM, TEAMS) via partners and cable operators in neighbouring countries, and lists cross-border fibre connection points with Rwanda (Gasenyi, Kanyaru Haut), the DRC (Ruhwa, Gatumba) and Tanzania (Kobero, Mugina/Manyovu); no per-route traffic or in-service dates are given, and no date is stated beyond the report's own (published 2021-07).
system: EASSy, SEACOM, TEAMS via Rwanda, DRC and Tanzania connection points
